newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua voters lack documents ahead of elections.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua voters lack documents ahead of elections.

text.p: A top election observer on Friday said he was worried by the slow pace of the voter documentation process heading into Nicaragua's Oct. 20 presidential election.

With just over one month before the landmark vote, 55 percent of Nicaragua's eligible voters still have not received the documents they need to vote, Oscar Santamaria, head of the Organisation of American States observer mission in Nicaragua, told Reuters.
"We're asking ourselves if it will be possible to give the necessary documents to all the people who are still without them by the elections," Santamaria said.
Santamaria said delays in printing voter identification cards had put enormous pressure on election officials to complete their distribution on time.
"There is still an enormous road to travel in this process, and they will have to make a super-extraordinary effort if all the people are going to be able to vote," he said.
Analysts have warned that if part of the population cannot vote, it may open the door to fraud charges if one political party says its supporters were intentionally denied voter cards.

Santamaria called the Oct. 20 vote "the most important election in Nicaragua's modern political history," and perhaps its first completely free election. The vote will mark the first time an elected civilian government hands over power to another such government in Nicaraguan history.
Nicaraguan election officials have had to overcome a series of technical problems affecting the electoral process.

Earlier this year they ran a massive campaign to register voters in remote regions of northern Nicaragua plagued by political violence where hundreds of thousands of voters had been left off registered lists.
Now they were trying to correct errors in the voters lists. Delays in the printing of the election ballots are threatening to cause another headache for election officials.
